comment_body:
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

This change disables the automated scroll-to-caret logic when the selection change is caused by a drag. While this prevents the viewport from incorrectly snapping to the `extent` handle when dragging the `base` handle (the "flickering" issue described), it also means that `EditableText` will no longer trigger any scrolling via this path during a drag.

If the intention is to rely entirely on the gesture detector (e.g., `TextSelectionGestureDetector`) to handle scrolling when a handle reaches the viewport edge, then this change is logically consistent. However, please note that the regression test added in this PR (line 4116 of `editable_text_test.dart`) appears to expect a scroll to occur when calling `userUpdateTextEditingValue` with `SelectionChangedCause.drag`. Since this code change specifically prevents that scroll, the test is likely to fail as written.

comment_body:
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

This expectation (`lessThan(initialOffset)`) indicates that the test expects the viewport to scroll upwards to follow the `base` handle. However, the changes in `editable_text.dart` specifically disable the call to `_scheduleShowCaretOnScreen` when the cause is `SelectionChangedCause.drag`.

Because this test calls `userUpdateTextEditingValue` directly rather than simulating a real drag gesture (which would trigger the gesture detector's own scrolling logic), no scroll will be triggered, and `scrollController.offset` will remain at `initialOffset`. This will cause the test to fail. To properly verify that the viewport follows a handle during a drag with the new changes, you should simulate a drag gesture using `tester.drag` or similar, which exercises the `TextSelectionGestureDetector` logic responsible for scrolling during active drags.

comment_body:
Looking into the history of this code block it seems that it was introduced to fix an issue where we would not auto scroll the text field to a visible position when first tapping on it https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/75604. At the time this change landed `_bringIntoViewBySelectionState` did not exist and was not called fom `formatAndSetValue`.

In it's current state `formatAndSetValue` does call `_bringIntoViewBySelectionState`. On iOS this handles both drags and long presses, while on Android only drags. 

The reason this bug is only presenting itself on Android and not iOS, is that when updating its selection, iOS always updates the moving edge to be the extent. Since `_scheduleShowCaretOnScreen` attempts to show the caret on screen (the extent of the selection), and we are always moving he extent, we always bring the moving edge into view as expected. On Android, if we move the start edge that is always going to move the `baseOffset` of the selection, similarly moving the end edge is always going to move the `extentOffset`. So when selecting backwards from the bottom of some long text, moving the start edge, `_scheduleShowCaretOnScreen` will always try to reveal the `extentOffset` even though we are moving the `baseOffset` and want to keep it in view.

A side note is that `TextFieldState._handleSelectionChanged` also calls `bringIntoView` when the selection changes because of a long press. Which would be called in `_handleSelectionChanged` before `_bringIntoViewBySelectionState` is called. These however do not conflict since on Android `_bringIntoViewBySelectionState` only handles drags and not long presses. On iOS we may be potentially calling `bringIntoView` twice. This should probably be addressed in a seperate PR.

> I wonder is the discrepancy between platforms intended?

Do you mean both platforms should set the dragged selection handle as the extent? My thought was that the platform difference was intentional. Checking Jetpack compose TextField and AndroidView EditText it seems that the current behavior with Android is still aligned, i.e. the dragged handle does not become the new extent. We make a lot of use of automatic conversion in constructing an integer object from a float object. That behavior isn't really specified and we should probably get rid of those automatic conversion constructors in favor of more responsible named factories. In this case, not only is the conversion from the the Size to the ISize unspecified, but the desired operation is either Round/Floor/Ceil and those operators exist directly on the Size object you get from GetSize() without having to "construct through" some other type.

In Skia (`ResolveTextureSkia`), `GrVkImageInfo` assumes the embedder has already placed the `VkImage` into `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL` without requiring an intermediate queue submission. Should we consider doing the same here? If so, we'd want to document in `embedder.h` that `VkImage` is expected to be in `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL` when provided to Flutter. If we add `external_format` (or `AHardwareBuffer` support) later, we can conditionally handle transitions here for textures that require them.

Updated in dc7181238de: `webgl.force-enabled: true` and `webgl.disable-fail-if-major-performance-caveat: true` remain enabled everywhere so Firefox requires WebGL, uses the hardware GPU when available locally, and falls back to software WebGL if no GPU is present. The software-forcing overrides (`gfx.webrender.software: true`, `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`, and container sandbox flags) are now gated strictly on `if (isCi)`.
